title: Quantized packet-plan Mirror latent
hypothesis: A small discrete Mirror packet-plan code can preserve joint future-mode coverage at lower actual bytes than a continuous packet latent and independent per-position predictions.
physical_object: one shared packet decoder over a fixed synthetic two-step transition model
mirror_coordinate: one discrete latent code selects a joint two-token future plan
logical_multiplicity: jointly decoded future packets under one shared decoder

development.allowed: choose codebook size from {2,4,8,16} on dev only

fresh.A0_excluded: exploratory due invalid mode table/coverage metric

success_gate: At some codebook size <=8, every fresh world covers >=95% of target joint modes and beats independent categorical coverage at <=50% of its payload bytes, without reducing valid packet rate.
failure_gate: Discrete code collisions reduce joint mode coverage or codebook/decoder bytes erase savings; report all mode-coverage and bit-rate tradeoffs.
boundaries: Synthetic branching packet task only; no language modeling or speculative decoding claim.
Logical combinations are not capacity; held-out joint mode coverage is authoritative.

amendment_A1.reason: A0 packet mode table accidentally used token IDs beyond the declared vocabulary and the coverage metric counted token symbols rather than distinct joint packet plans. A0 preserved as exploratory and excluded.
amendment_A1.change: Use 16 unique legal joint pairs over an 8-symbol vocabulary; joint-mode coverage counts distinct plan codes and independent valid rate sums probability over legal pairs. No gate change.
